# pbs_disks (Data Source)

Lists the disks of a Proxmox Backup Server node, as its interface shows them under Storage / Disks: what each is used for, its size, model and serial number and, when asked for, its SMART health and its partitions. PBS lists the whole disks the kernel names as SCSI, SATA, IDE, virtio or Xen disks (`sda`, `hda`, `vda`, `xvda`) or as NVMe namespaces (`nvme0n1`); it leaves out loop, device-mapper, software RAID (`md`) and SD card (`mmcblk`) devices, and iSCSI disks.

Needs `Sys.Audit on /system/disks`.

PBS runs `lsblk` and `pvs` to tell what the disks are used for, and reading fails when either does. A PBS in a container lists the host's disks it sees in `/sys/block`; without udev's database (`/run/udev`) it cannot tell their `model`, `serial`, `wwn` and `rpm`, which are null then, nor their partition tables, so that `gpt` is `false`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pbs_disks" "unused" {
  usage_type = "unused"
}

# Disks free for a new datastore, such as ["/dev/sdb", "/dev/sdc"].
output "unused_disks" {
  value = [for d in data.pbs_disks.unused.disks : d.devpath]
}

# SMART health of every disk. PBS runs smartctl on each, which takes a while
# and wakes disks that are spun down.
data "pbs_disks" "smart" {
  smart = true
}

check "disks_are_healthy" {
  assert {
    condition     = alltrue([for d in data.pbs_disks.smart.disks : d.health != "failed"])
    error_message = "SMART reports failing disks: ${join(", ", [for d in data.pbs_disks.smart.disks : d.name if d.health == "failed"])}."
  }
}

# Disks with less than a fifth of their rated life left. HDDs report no
# wear; neither does an NVMe disk used beyond its rated life, which is listed
# too when SMART answered for it.
output "worn_disks" {
  value = [
    for d in data.pbs_disks.smart.disks : d.name
    if d.wearout != null ? d.wearout < 20 : startswith(d.name, "nvme") && d.health != "unknown"
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `include_partitions` (Boolean) Whether to list the partitions of each disk in `partitions`. Defaults to `false`.
- `node` (String) Node to read: `localhost` or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`.
- `smart` (Boolean) Whether to read the SMART data of the disks, for `health` and `wearout`. PBS then runs `smartctl` on every disk, four at a time and without a timeout, which can take long with many disks and wakes those that are spun down. Defaults to `false`, which leaves `health` `unknown` and `wearout` null.
- `usage_type` (String) List only the disks used so, as `used` names it: `unused`, `mounted`, `lvm`, `zfs`, `devicemapper`, `partitions` or `filesystem`. Every disk when left out.

### Read-Only

- `disks` (Attributes List) The disks, sorted by name. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--disks))

<a id="nestedatt--disks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `disks`

Read-Only:

- `devpath` (String) Path of the disk's device node, such as `/dev/sda`; null when it has none.
- `disk_type` (String) Kind of disk, as PBS guesses it: `ssd` or `hdd` by whether the kernel reports it as rotational, which virtual disks often are; `usb` or `unknown` when the kernel does not say.
- `gpt` (Boolean) Whether the disk has a GPT partition table, as udev reports it; `false` without udev's data.
- `health` (String) SMART health of the disk, as `smartctl` reports it: `passed`, `failed` or `unknown`. Always `unknown` without `smart`, and for a disk whose health `smartctl` cannot read, such as most virtual disks.
- `model` (String) Model of the disk, as udev reports it, such as `Samsung_SSD_870_EVO_1TB`; null without udev's data.
- `name` (String) Kernel name of the disk, such as `sda` or `nvme0n1`.
- `partitions` (Attributes List) The partitions of the disk, in partition order: `sda2` before `sda10`. Empty without `include_partitions`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--disks--partitions))
- `rpm` (Number) Rotation rate of an ATA disk, in revolutions per minute, as udev reports it: `0` for one that does not rotate, such as an SSD. Null for other disks, and without udev's data.
- `serial` (String) Serial number of the disk, as udev reports it; null without udev's data.
- `size` (Number) Size of the disk, in bytes.
- `used` (String) What PBS finds the disk used for: `mounted` (a file system on it or on one of its partitions is mounted), `lvm` (it or a partition is an LVM physical volume), `zfs` (it or a partition is in a ZFS pool), `devicemapper` (another device, such as a device-mapper or software RAID device, is built on it or a partition), `partitions` (it has partitions, none of them in use), `filesystem` (it holds a file system that is not mounted) or `unused`.
- `vendor` (String) Vendor of the disk, as the kernel reports it, such as `ATA` for a SATA disk; null when it reports none.
- `wearout` (Number) Percentage of the disk's rated life left, from SMART: for an NVMe disk, 100 minus the percentage used it reports; for an ATA disk, the normalised value of its wear attribute, such as `Media_Wearout_Indicator`. Null without `smart`, for a disk that reports no wear, such as most HDDs, and for an NVMe disk used beyond its rated life.
- `wwn` (String) World Wide Name of the disk, as udev reports it, such as `0x5002538f42a1b2c3`; null when the disk has none, and without udev's data.

<a id="nestedatt--disks--partitions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `disks.partitions`

Read-Only:

- `devpath` (String) Path of the partition's device node, such as `/dev/sda1`; null when it has none.
- `filesystem` (String) Type of the file system on the partition, as `lsblk` reports it, such as `ext4`; null unless `used` is `filesystem`.
- `gpt` (Boolean) Whether udev reports a GPT partition table for the partition; `false` without udev's data.
- `mounted` (Boolean) Whether a file system on the partition is mounted.
- `name` (String) Kernel name of the partition, such as `sda1` or `nvme0n1p1`.
- `size` (Number) Size of the partition, in bytes; null when PBS cannot read it.
- `used` (String) What PBS finds the partition used for: `lvm` (an LVM physical volume), `zfs` (in a ZFS pool), `zfsreserved` (the reserved partition ZFS makes on a whole disk), `efi` (an EFI system partition), `bios` (a BIOS boot partition), `filesystem` (it holds a file system) or `unused`.
- `uuid` (String) UUID of the file system on the partition, as `lsblk` reports it; null when it has none, or one that is not in the usual UUID form, such as the volume ID of a FAT file system.
